processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Samples melted and cast in a VIM furnace under 400 mbar Ar pressure; five Cu molds moved stepwise and filled from a 4-kg ingot, with Al charged through an air lock after each cast.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets reheated to 1100 °C and water quenched, then cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments of 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Homogenization performed at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching; no subsequent aging (0 h aging, as-homogenized state).

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained microsegregations of Mn; no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens prepared from segments by package spark erosion; cross-sections prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: all plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: mechanical behavior (YS, UTS, TE) across aging conditions

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements for every material state
characterization_methods.key_findings: 360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE for the as-homogenized Fe-30Mn-1.2C reference state

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: HBW scale; plotted in Fig. 3d for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl series
characterization_methods.key_findings: hardness nearly flat around 200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al (0Al as-homogenized ≈ 200 HBW)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques
characterization_methods.key_findings: no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations; as-cast samples coarse dendritic; after hot rolling and water quenching fully recrystallized with ~20 µm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations

unmapped_findings: The Fe-30Mn-1.2C (0 wt.% Al) alloy is the Al-free reference material of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP screening; in the as-homogenized state it shows the best mechanical behavior of that alloy (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE), while aging reduces UTS and TE and embrittlement becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and temperatures above 500 °C.

The alloy classifies as a single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel: for Al contents below 5 wt.% a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature and the TWIP effect (dislocation hardening followed by mechanical twinning) is the primary strain-hardening mechanism.

The paper presents a temperature-sensitive constitutive strain-hardening model for low-SFE fcc TWIP steels that is applicable in principle to SIMPLEX-type compositions such as this Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy, but no model run or experimental validation specific to this as-homogenized Fe-30Mn-1.2C sample is reported.
